hyperedges.label: Five-Part Voice Assistant Architecture (brain, hands, ears/mouth, memory, heartbeat)
Thin Provider Seam Pattern (model, STT, TTS)

nodes.label: Always-On Host for the Heartbeat
nodes.rationale: Laptop-first to start, but the loop is designed not to care which machine it runs on so time-based help can fire while the laptop sleeps - a relocation, not a rewrite.

nodes.label: Background Heartbeat Loop
nodes.rationale: A lightweight loop separate from the conversation loop, wakes on an interval, runs checks and routes noteworthy results to one place; kept cleanly separable so relocating it to an always-on machine is a move, not a rewrite.

nodes.label: Configuration File Over Hardcoded Values
nodes.rationale: Thresholds, intervals, quiet hours, model name, voice choice and which tools require confirmation are tuned often, so changing them should be a one-line edit rather than a code change.

nodes.label: Kill Switch
nodes.rationale: One obvious way to pause all proactive behavior without tearing anything down - wanted the first time the assistant does something unexpected, not after.

nodes.label: No Overlapping Check Runs
nodes.rationale: Skip a new run while the previous one is still working so slow checks do not snowball.

nodes.label: Quiet Hours
nodes.rationale: Non-urgent surfacing waits for waking hours; the quiet window is a setting, and only truly critical items earn a late-night interruption.

nodes.label: Scheduled Checks
nodes.rationale: Each check is its own unit - when it runs, what it looks at, how it decides whether the outcome is worth surfacing - with what-to-check and how-often kept in config because they are tuned constantly.

nodes.label: Specialist Sub-Agents
nodes.rationale: Big jobs are handed to a sub-agent with its own prompt and tools that reports back; the tool registry and heartbeat are the seams that make this natural rather than a rewrite.

nodes.label: Tier 5 - The Heartbeat (proactivity)
nodes.rationale: The leap from a thing you talk to into a thing that helps you; also the tier where a careless build becomes annoying, hence quiet by default.

nodes.label: Catch-Up-on-Return Delivery
nodes.rationale: Notices raised while the interface is closed must be held and shown on return rather than fired into the void; deliver-once-and-lose-it is the most common way a proactive feature silently fails.

nodes.label: Never Block Forever Waiting on a Human
nodes.norm_label: never block forever waiting on a human
nodes.rationale: A background action awaiting approval must time out into a safe default (do nothing, leave a note) or the loop deadlocks and quietly stops working unnoticed.

nodes.label: Quiet by Default
nodes.rationale: It earns interruptions rather than assuming them; most checks produce nothing most of the time, everything else accumulates in a calm log. A proactive assistant that cries wolf gets muted, and a muted assistant is useless.

nodes.label: Interruptible Speech (barge-in)
nodes.rationale: Starting a new turn mid-reply must stop playback and listen; an assistant that will not let you cut it off feels broken fast.

nodes.label: ElevenLabs (text-to-speech)
nodes.rationale: Chosen for natural voices that make the assistant feel like a presence rather than a robot reading, and because it streams so playback can start before synthesis finishes. Voice choice belongs in the config file, not hardcoded.

nodes.label: Push-to-Talk Capture
nodes.rationale: Most reliable and cheapest path to get right: you never have to guess when speech started or finished, and it sidesteps the assistant hearing itself. Wake words come later.

nodes.label: Streaming Model Replies
nodes.rationale: Makes the text version feel alive and is a prerequisite for Tier 3 so the assistant can start speaking before it has finished thinking.

nodes.label: Tier 1 - The Brain (text conversation loop)
nodes.rationale: Smallest possible loop - read input, append to history, send history plus system prompt, print and append reply - proves memory-within-session before any other layer exists.

nodes.label: Tier 2 - The Hands (tool calling)
nodes.rationale: Without tools the assistant can only talk; with them it can act. The loop must allow several tool calls in a row before the model answers.

nodes.label: Tier 3 - The Ears and Mouth (voice in, voice out)
nodes.norm_label: tier 3 - the ears and mouth (voice in, voice out)
nodes.rationale: Wraps the existing loop rather than rewriting it - only the two ends of a turn change; forking agent logic for voice is explicitly a wrong turn.

nodes.label: Show the Transcript Next to the Reply
nodes.norm_label: show the transcript next to the reply
nodes.rationale: Transcription will mishear; printing what it thought you said reveals whether the ears or the brain was at fault.

nodes.label: Latency Is the Whole Experience
nodes.rationale: Every stage adds delay, so stream at every stage, start speaking early, and show an immediate sign on key release so silence never reads as breakage.

nodes.label: One Shared Agent Core, Many Ways In and Out
nodes.norm_label: one shared agent core, many ways in and out
nodes.rationale: A typed turn, a spoken turn and a heartbeat-initiated turn must all flow through the same brain; writing agent logic twice (text and voice) is the signal to stop and unify.

nodes.label: Speech Synthesis Seam
nodes.rationale: One small function - give me text, play it aloud - so the voice or the provider changes in one place.

nodes.label: Hard Confirmation Gate
nodes.rationale: Sits between the model choosing a tool and the tool running so it covers spoken, typed and heartbeat-initiated actions alike; irreversible actions never proceed on assumed permission.

nodes.label: Graceful Model Failure Handling
nodes.rationale: Network calls fail; a daily-driver assistant must show a clear message and a clean prompt rather than a stack trace.

nodes.label: Per-Tool Safety Classification
nodes.rationale: Read-only lookups may run freely; anything that sends, spends, deletes or changes a setting is flagged at Tier 2 so the Tier 6 gate can stop it.

nodes.label: Tier 6 - The Rails (safety, confirmation, configuration)
nodes.rationale: Less new machinery than a posture applied across everything already built, so the assistant is trustworthy enough to leave running.

nodes.label: Tool Registry
nodes.rationale: Each tool registered with a name, a one-line description of when to use it and typed inputs; the whole registry is handed to the model each turn. Adding a capability means writing one self-contained tool, never editing the core loop - that is what lets the assistant grow without becoming tangled.

nodes.label: Typed, Validated Tool Inputs
nodes.rationale: Named typed inputs instead of freeform blobs mean fewer wrong calls and far easier debugging.

nodes.label: Treat Ingested Content as Data, Not Commands
nodes.norm_label: treat ingested content as data, not commands
nodes.rationale: Web pages, emails, files and transcripts may contain text shaped like instructions; valid instructions come only from the user in conversation, and suspicious content is surfaced rather than obeyed. This matters more as tools reach the internet.

nodes.label: Stored Memory Is Data, Not Instructions
nodes.norm_label: stored memory is data, not instructions
nodes.rationale: A stored note that reads like an order must still pass normal judgment and the confirmation rules, so memory never becomes a backdoor around the Tier 6 safety gate.

nodes.label: Confirmation Is Per-Action and Does Not Generalize
nodes.norm_label: confirmation is per-action and does not generalize
nodes.rationale: Approving one send does not pre-authorize the next; mildly more friction is what makes the assistant safe to let off the leash.

nodes.label: Describe Tools for a Reader, Not a Compiler
nodes.norm_label: describe tools for a reader, not a compiler
nodes.rationale: The model picks tools by description; vague names cause wrong calls or no call at all.

nodes.label: Return Tool Errors to the Model
nodes.norm_label: return tool errors to the model
nodes.rationale: Catch failures and return a plain-language error to the model instead of crashing; the agent reasoning over a failed tool result is a feature, not a bug.

nodes.label: Visible Audit Trail
nodes.rationale: A plain log of which tools ran, what the heartbeat surfaced and what was confirmed is how surprises get diagnosed; a running model-cost tally makes a runaway loop immediately visible.

nodes.label: Deepgram (speech-to-text)
nodes.rationale: Chosen for the reference build because it is fast, accurate and streams, keeping the gap between key release and understanding short.

nodes.label: Dismissible Surfaced Items
nodes.rationale: An inbox of proactive notices that cannot be cleared becomes clutter the user starts ignoring.

nodes.label: Secrets Out of Code
nodes.rationale: API keys (model, Deepgram, ElevenLabs) live in environment variables or a git-ignored secrets file from the very first commit; never pasted into source even temporarily.

nodes.label: A Face (visual interface)
nodes.rationale: Turns the audit log and dismissible notices into something glanced at instead of read.

nodes.label: Human-Readable, User-Editable Memory
nodes.rationale: Memory you cannot inspect is memory you cannot trust, so the store stays plain enough to open, fix or delete by hand.

nodes.label: Model Provider Seam
nodes.rationale: One small function - send this conversation, get back a reply or a tool request - so models can be swapped and retries and cost logging added in one place; nothing else touches the provider SDK.

nodes.label: Transcription Seam
nodes.rationale: One small function - give me audio, get back text - so the transcriber can be switched without touching the rest of the harness.

nodes.label: graphify explain
nodes.rationale: Used for focused single-concept questions.

nodes.label: Graphify Knowledge Graph
nodes.rationale: A persistent graph at graphify-out/ with god nodes, community structure and cross-file relationships exists so codebase questions resolve against a scoped subgraph instead of raw grep output.

nodes.label: graphify path
nodes.rationale: Used for relationship questions between two named entities.

nodes.label: graphify query
nodes.rationale: First tool for codebase questions because it returns a scoped subgraph, usually much smaller than GRAPH_REPORT.md or raw grep output.

nodes.label: graphify update
nodes.rationale: Run after modifying code to keep the graph current; AST-only so there is no API cost.

nodes.label: GRAPH_REPORT.md
nodes.rationale: Reserved for broad architecture review or when query/path/explain do not surface enough context, because it is large compared to a scoped subgraph.

nodes.label: Graphify Wiki Index
nodes.rationale: Preferred over raw source browsing for broad navigation when graphify-out/wiki/index.md exists.

nodes.label: Durable Schedule State
nodes.rationale: Persist when each check is next due so a restart does not reset timers or fire everything at once on boot.

nodes.label: Long-Term Memory Store
nodes.rationale: A simple durable store read at conversation start and written to during one, loaded into the system prompt, with tools to record, update and remove facts so the assistant manages its own memory.

nodes.label: Tier 4 - The Memory (durable across restarts)
nodes.rationale: In-session history from Tier 1 is short-term; this long-term store survives restart so the assistant greets you like it knows you.

nodes.label: One Fact Per Entry
nodes.rationale: Small legible entries are easy to review, correct and delete; a giant blob of everything known about the user rots quickly and is impossible to audit.

nodes.label: Selective Memory Loading
nodes.rationale: Loading everything is fine early, but design so retrieval can become relevance-scoped as the store grows rather than dumping it into every prompt.

nodes.label: Trillion (reference assistant name)
nodes.rationale: Placeholder name used in the document until the user picks their own; the name surfaces in greetings, logs and the later wake phrase.

nodes.label: Voice-First AI Assistant Harness
nodes.rationale: The goal is a real dependable assistant built as a harness around a language model, not a chatbot demo; described as experience and engineering approach with deliberately no code so the implementer chooses stack while matching structure, priorities and safety posture.

nodes.label: Keep the Text Path Alive Forever
nodes.norm_label: keep the text path alive forever
nodes.rationale: The typed interface is how every future change gets debugged without talking to the computer, and it is a graceful fallback when audio misbehaves.

nodes.label: Get the Brain Working in Text Before Audio
nodes.norm_label: get the brain working in text before audio
nodes.rationale: Stated as the single most important rule of the whole build: voice is a layer on top of a working agent, never the foundation.

nodes.label: Tier-by-Tier Incremental Build Discipline
nodes.rationale: Each tier ends in something runnable with a verification step so layers are independently testable; a voice assistant has many moving parts and debugging them all at once is miserable.

nodes.label: Never-Without-Asking List
nodes.rationale: Collected during the interview (default: anything that sends, spends, deletes or changes a setting) so the Tier 6 confirmation rule has teeth from the beginning.

nodes.label: System Prompt
nodes.rationale: Carries the assistant's name, interview-chosen personality and purpose statement, and later the loaded long-term memory facts, so tone stays consistent everywhere.

nodes.label: Tier 0 - Interview First
nodes.rationale: Ask identity, stack and boundary questions in one grouped round before writing code, using stated defaults for skipped answers, so the build has a single source of truth from the start.

nodes.label: AGENT.md Spec File
nodes.rationale: A short plain-language spec at the project root gives the rest of the build and any future session a single source of truth for what is being built and why.

hyperedges.label: Five-Part Voice Assistant Architecture (brain, hands, ears/mouth, memory, heartbeat)
Thin Provider Seam Pattern (model, STT, TTS)
